CLCON No. 346 of 2023
Hon’ble Ravindra Maithani, J.
Mr. Dushyant Mainali, Advocate for 
the petitioner.
Mr. J.S. Bisht, Brief Holder for the 
State.
This matter was heard alongwith 
WPCRL No. 1655 of 2023.
According to the petitioner, it is case 
of the contemnor. The petitioner was 
arrested on false grounds in defiance to 
the directions of the Hon’ble Supreme 
Court laid down in the case of Arnesh 
Kumar Vs. State of Bihar, (2014) 8 SCC 
273 as well as the arrest of the petitioner 
was made in defiance to the circular No. 
315/UHC/Admin-B/V-a-7-2014 dated 
04.09.2023.
During the course of hearing 
learned counsel for the petitioner would 
submit that the petitioner is Manager of 
the resort. The police wanted rooms free
of cost. On one occasion, it could not be 
provided because the rooms had already 
been booked for the marriage. Therefore, 
the police became annoyed and a false 
case has been lodged. The arrest was 
made in defiance of the guidelines given 
by the Hon’ble Supreme Court in the case 
of Arnesh Kumar (supra) as well as the 
circular of this Court dated 04.09.2023. 
It is also argued that the resort people are 
much scared of the Police. The SHO of 
the police station was suspended, but 
within three days he was reinstated and 
he is still there. The Court wanted to know about it,
from the learned State counsel. He would 
submit that he has no idea about it.
In the instant matter, the date is 
already fixed for 11.01.2024.
State has already been required to 
file objection.
If there are such allegations against 
the police of which judicial notice has 
been taken by the Court in WPCRL No. 
1655 of 2023 and the instant petition, 
why should the same police officer be 
permitted to continue in the area where 
the resort falls? Could not it be an act of 
perpetuating those alleged wrong? Does 
not the concept of clean governance and 
the rule of law may require that such 
police officers may be transferred to some 
other police station quite at a distance 
from the place where the resort falls? 
Could not it be good for both, the 
contemnor as well as the petitioner? The 
Court leaves it to the wisdom of the 
senior police officers and would examine 
this issue, if occasion arises on 
11.01.2024.
List this matter on the date already 
fixed.
 (Ravindra Maithani, J.)
 27.12.2023 Jitendra

CLCON No. 346 of 2023
Hon’ble Ravindra Maithani, J.
Mr. Dushyant Mainali, Advocate for the 
petitioners.
Mr. C.S. Rawat, Chief Standing Counsel 
for the State.
Mr. Vipul Sharma, Advocate for the 
respondent no.2.
Mr. Lalit Sharma, Advocate for the 
respondent nos. 3.
A report is received from the Deputy 
Inspector General of Police, Kumaon Division.
 According to the petitioner, rooms in the 
resort were demanded by the sub-ordinate of 
for his guests of contemnor/respondent no.1. 
The report says that the contemnor/respondent 
no.1 did not make any request.
Whether, the Deputy Inspector General, 
Police made any inquiry, as to who made the 
‘WhatsApp chats’? What was the basis of 
those chats? How could a subordinate of the 
contemnor/respondent no.1 demand for a room 
in a resort in the name of the 
contemnor/respondent no.1? Were there any 
guests coming on those days? Had they come? 
Where did they stay? How the sub-ordinate 
could make a demand in the name the 
contemnor/respondent no.1 without the 
direction of the contemnor/respondent no.1? If 
such inquiry was not made, how it can be 
recorded that demand was not made by the 
contemnor/respondent no.1? Why the 
contemnor/respondent no.1 was posted in the 
same police station again where there are 
allegations that he had falsely implicated the 
resort owner and its employees and committed 
contempt of the Court?
When asked, learned Chief Standing 
Counsel seeks time.
List on 19.12.2024 at 2:00 PM along with 
connected matter. The Court requests the Deputy Inspector 
General of Police, Kumaon Division to also join 
the proceedings through video conferencing.
Let a copy of this order be sent to the 
Director General of Police as well as Deputy 
Inspector General of Police, Kumaon Division,
today itself, through e-mail/FAX for 
information and necessary action.
 (Ravindra Maithani, J.) 
 18.12.2024
Jitendra

Dr. Yogendra Singh Rawat, Deputy
Inspector General, Kumaon Division, 
Nainital is present through video 
conferencing. 
On 18.12.2024, this Court had 
requested the Deputy Inspector General of 
Police, Kumaon Division, Nainital to assist 
the Court on certain aspects. On that date, 
the Court passed the following orders:- 
 “A report is received from the 
Deputy Inspector General of Police, 
Kumaon Division. 
 According to the petitioner, 
rooms in the resort were demanded by 
the sub-ordinate of for his guests of 
contemnor/respondent no. 1. The 
report says that the 
contemnor/respondent no. 1 did not 
make any request.
 Whether, the Deputy Inspector 
General, Police made any inquiry, as 
to who made the ‘WhatsApp chats’? 
What was the basis of those chats? 
How could a subordinate of the 
contemnor/respondent no. 1 demand 
for a room in a resort in the name of 
the guests coming on those days? Had 
they come? Where did they stay? How 
the sub-ordinate could make a  demand in the name of the 
contemnor/respondent no. 1 without 
the direction of the 
contemnor/respondent no. 1? If such 
inquiry was not made, how it can be 
recorded that demand was not made 
by the contemnor/respondent no. 1? 
Why the contemnor/respondent no. 1 
was posted in the same police station 
again where there are allegations that 
he had falsely implicated the resort 
owner and its employees and 
committed contempt of the Court?
 When asked, learned Chief 
Standing Counsel seeks time.
 List on 19.12.2024 at 2:00 PM 
along with connected matter. 
 The Court requests the Deputy 
Inspector General of Police, Kumaon 
Division to also join the proceedings 
through video conferencing.
 Let a copy of this order be 
sent to the Director General of Police 
as well as Deputy Inspector General of 
Police, Kumaon Division, today itself, 
through e-mail/FAX for information 
and necessary action. ”
Dr. Yogendra Singh Rawat, Deputy 
Inspector General of Police, Kumaon
Division, Nainital assisted the Court. 
The Deputy Inspector General of 
Police submits that he would further 
examine this matter and would decide as to 
what is to be done.
Let a copy of the supplementary 
affidavit dated 15.12.2023 in connected 
WPCRL No. 1655 of 2022 be also supplied 
to the learned Chief Standing Counsel for 
its further transmission to the Deputy 
Inspector General of Police, Kumaon
Division, Nainital.
List on 16.02.2025.
 
 (Ravindra Maithani J.) 
19.12.2024

Hon’ble Ravindra Maithani, J.
Mr. G. C. Lakhchaura, Advocate and Mr. 
Dushyant Mainali, Advocate through video 
conferencing for the petitioners.
Ms. Manisha Rana Singh, D.A.G. for the 
State in WPCRL No. 1655 of 2023
Mr. Vipul Sharma, Advocate for the 
respondent no.2 in CLCON No. 346 of 2023
Mr. Lalit Sharma, Advocate for the 
respondent no. 3 in CLCON No. 346 of 2023.
Mr. Devesh Ghildiyal, Standing Counsel 
for the State in CLCON No. 346 of 2023.
Supplementary affidavits and counter 
affidavits are taken on record. IA No. 1 of 2023, 
IA No. 2 of 2024, IA No. 3 of 2024 and IA No. 4 
of 2024 stand disposed of accordingly.
In this petition, there are multiple 
allegations against the police officers with 
regard to manipulation of the records, 
malafide, forgery, illegal arrest etc. One of the 
allegations is that when illegally the resort was 
raided by the police officers, they took the DVR 
out and did not return it.
Now a supplementary affidavit dated 
02.03.2025 has been filed by the petitioners 
enclosing conversation between the Asif Khan, 
the Investigating Officer (“the IO”) with Hariom 
Sharma, who, it is stated is father of the 
petitioner no.2, which records that, in fact, on 
the date of conversation, the DVR was in the  custody of the IO, Asif Khan.
Let IO, Asif Khan file a short affidavit 
stating as to where is that DVR? How he get 
custody of it? What was the occasion for him to 
speak to Hariom Sharma on 13.12.2013? Has 
the DVR been sent for forensic examination? If 
yes, when?
This affidavit shall be filed within a week.
List on 17.07.2026 after fresh cases.
This Court requests learned State counsel 
to ensure that this order is communicated to 
the IO, Asif Khan and he files his affidavit 
within time.
 (Ravindra Maithani, J.) 
 10.07.2026
Jitendra
